articles.title: One Interface, Three Search Backends: Web Search Is Just Another Repository
articles.excerpt: If you build anything with LLMs, you will need web search sooner or later. The model's training data is frozen; your users' questions are not. In Solon AI, web search is not a special subsystem bolted…
articles.body: If you build anything with LLMs, you will need web search sooner or later. The model's training data is frozen; your users' questions are not. In Solon AI, web search is not a special subsystem bolted onto the side. It is a Repository — the same interface a vector store implements, the same interface an in-memory document list implements. That single design decision is the whole story of the solon-ai-rag-searchs family, and it composes in ways you might not expect.

articles.title: When Agent Chains Run for Hours: Why Checkpointing Is the Real Challenge
articles.excerpt: Today's GitHub Trending tells an interesting story. morluto/rea uses agent chains to reverse engineer anything "from app behavior down to native binaries." boykopovar/AnyPS5 automates PS5 executable p…
articles.body: Today's GitHub Trending tells an interesting story. morluto/rea uses agent chains to reverse engineer anything "from app behavior down to native binaries." boykopovar/AnyPS5 automates PS5 executable porting to Linux and Windows. Both are impressive — and both represent a class of problems that few people are talking about: long-running, multi-step agent workflows . The Problem Nobody Talks About When your agent chain runs for hours across dozens of steps, the real enemy isn't model capability. It's what happens when step 7 of 12 fails at minute 90. Do you start over? That's hours of computation wasted. Do you retry just that step? How do you know the previous steps' outputs are still valid? How do you persist intermediate state across failures?

articles.body: If you build anything that needs eBay sold prices, 2026 broke your stack twice. Here is the current state of every route to completed listings data, and working code for the one that still works. Full disclosure up front: I run CompsAPI, which is one of the options below. The rest of this post is accurate whether or not you use it. What actually happened A short timeline, because half the tutorials online are now wrong: 2020 : eBay deprecates findCompletedItems , the Finding API call everyone used for sold listings. February 2025 : the whole Finding API is decommissioned. Code that called it gets security errors, not data. The official replacement, the Marketplace Insights API , is a limited release. You apply with a business case, and approval is restricted to established eBay partners.

articles.body: Many software developers and AI engineers build impressive projects, solve complex technical problems, and experiment with new technologies. However, the lessons they learn from these projects are not always documented or shared with the wider technical community. There are several ways developers can make their technical work more visible. Document your experiments When working on an AI or machine learning project, explain the problem you wanted to solve, the approach you used, and what you learned. Documenting your process helps other developers understand your work and reproduce your results. Write technical articles A well-written article can explain a new implementation, compare different approaches, or discuss the limitations of an existing solution.

articles.excerpt: Smart assist would clean up your messy speech before translating.
articles.body: TL;DR Google introduced Rambler for Gboard earlier this year, removing filler words and cleaning up your voice input for text conversion. Now Google Translate appears to be preparing its own similar mode called Smart assist. It’s not yet clear if Smart assist would have some of the same limitations as Rambler. Voice-to-text sounds like a great idea… until you actually listen closely to how people really speak. While we expect the written word to be clear and formal, speech is often anything but — and that’s exactly why we have tools like Rambler in Gboard , able to compensate for our messy utterances. Now Google Translate looks like it could be cooking up a similar system of its own. You’re reading an Authority Insights story.
